messages:
maya: Customer reported streaming session that disconnects after ~35s, then client immediately reconnects and gets only partial output. Correlation:  e2f7a9c4.

sam: Which LB in front of their origin? ALB or NLB? Any Cloudflare in the path?

maya: They have NLB -> envoy ingress (our private deployment). No Cloudflare.

alex: Seen this pattern before when TCP idle probes vs HTTP keepalive disagree. Does the client TCP FIN or is it a half-close from server?

maya: Packet capture shows server still sending, then NLB sends RST to client, client opens new conn and sends auth token. New conn hits different backend that has stale auth cache and immediately returns 401, so client bails.

sam: Interesting — so two problems: NLB is tearing connection mid-stream (buffering/idle?) and our auth cache mismatch across backends on reconnect.

jordan: Do we have a repro? Any minimal steps we can give ops?

maya: Repro steps from customer: 1) Start SSE stream with token A. 2) Let it idle ~30s (no tokens emitted) to trigger NLB idle window. 3) Resume stream on server side (server writes). 4) NLB sends RST to client, client reconnects with token B (rotated) -> sometimes hits different envoy pod where auth cache hasn't updated -> 401.

sam: Can you paste the envoy upstream healthcheck / connection logs? Also need NLB idle timeout value.

maya: NLB idle timeout is default 35000ms. Envoy logs attached (snip):

```
[2026-02-19T15:02:11Z] connection id=592 accepted from 10.0.0.1:52344
[2026-02-19T15:02:46Z] stream id=314 write 0 bytes -> idle
[2026-02-19T15:02:46Z] tcp reset sent to 10.0.0.5:52344 by NLB
[2026-02-19T15:02:46Z] new connection id=593 from 10.0.0.1:52345
[2026-02-19T15:02:47Z] auth check token=A -> ok
[2026-02-19T15:02:47Z] auth cache refresh scheduled
[2026-02-19T15:02:47Z] auth check token=B -> denied
```

alex: That line `tcp reset sent ... by NLB` is the smoking gun. NLB is enforcing TCP idle and closing before server emits. When the client reconnects the session-affinity isn't preserved so token mismatch occurs.

oncall-bot: @support oncall triggered (sam) — paging for mitigation steps.

sam: Short-term mitigations: 1) Increase NLB idle timeout > expected gap (e.g., 120s). 2) Use session affinity (source IP) for NLB or configure sticky target group so reconnect lands on same backend. 3) Make auth tolerant to token rotation for short windows (accept previous token for X seconds).

jordan: Long-term: add SSE-specific keepalive heartbeats at client side every 15s to prevent idle, or server should send a small 1-byte comment chunk periodically. Also change routing so reconnects prefer same pod (cookie/sourceip).

maya: Customer tried client heartbeat but their mobile client suspends timers when backgrounded. They want server-side fixes.

sam: For Private deployments we can recommend 3 config changes: NLB idle timeout bump, enable source-ip affinity, and tweak envoy idle timeouts to match. I'll open a config doc.

alex: Also log correlation id on auth cache updates and implement a quick cache flush endpoint for ops to force-refresh auth entries when a token rotates.

maya: I've forwarded mitigation list to the customer and opened a support ticket with steps + recommended config. They asked for a reproducible test harness.

jordan: I can spin up a small repro: NLB -> envoy docker compose simulating token rotation + idle writes. Will post results.

sam: Thanks. If we get repro, let's document exact packet traces and add a KB article: "SSE disconnects due to NLB idle + token rotation".

maya: Good plan. Closing loop when jordan posts repro link. :thumbsup:
